info.name: ACME Water Utility Customer App (AWUCA)
info.description:
Customer-facing API for the ACME Water Utility Customer App.

This collection is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the harness:

  * Prism mocks it directly (Prism reads Postman Collections natively).
  * The Playwright @contract suite is generated from it at runtime.
  * The Python backend in /python-backend implements it.

Paths are pinned by /edge/kvs/routing.yaml. The CloudFront Function rewrites
/pay -> /v1/payments/methods, /bill -> /v1/billing/statement and
/join -> /v1/loyalty/signup, so those three paths must not be renamed without
editing the rewrite table in the same change.

Workload split follows README section 2A: everything is a mock ECS task except
the Loyalty folder, which is a mock Lambda.

Bodies use lorem ipsum. Per ai/tasks/apps.md the point is the development
paradigm, not the fidelity of the data.


SEEDED DEMO DATA

Every customer is seeded identically on first token issue. The examples below
describe that seed, so the generated contract suite is satisfiable against a
real implementation and not only against a mock.

  * Accounts acc-0001 .. acc-000N, where N is the x-account-count sent at
    token issue. The last is `closed` when N >= 3; the rest are `open`.
  * Payment methods pm-0001 (card, default) and pm-0002 (direct debit).
  * Loyalty: acc-0001 is ENROLLED, acc-0002 is NOT.
  * Closure: acc-0001 has a Pending request, acc-0002 has none.


TWO EXAMPLES, TWO REQUESTS

Where an endpoint documents both a success and a not-found example, the two
must differ in their REQUEST, not merely in the state of the world. One
account cannot be both enrolled and not enrolled, so a pair of identical
requests with different responses is unsatisfiable for any real backend and
only ever passes against a mock. That is why loyalty enrolment is keyed by
accountId and why the closure examples use different accounts.

Keep this property when adding examples.

item.name: Loyalty
item.description:
Purpose 6.

WORKLOAD: mock AWS Lambda, not ECS. Per README section 2A every route except loyalty is a mock ECS task; loyalty is the Lambda. It is reached through the same ALB listeners and promoted by the same atomic swap, so it is indistinguishable from an ECS route to the caller.

PATH IS PINNED: /edge/kvs/routing.yaml rewrites /join to /v1/loyalty/signup and the legacy /v1/loyalty-program-11 to /v1/loyalty.

request.description:
Set the loyalty ID. Enrol the account and mint a loyalty programme ID.

IDEMPOTENT: signing up an already-enrolled account returns 201 with the existing enrolment rather than a conflict. This is what keeps the example satisfiable against the seeded data, where acc-0001 is already enrolled, and it makes the request safe to retry.

Get the loyalty ID for one of the customer's accounts.

Enrolment is per account, matching the accountId that Sign Up accepts and returns. That also keeps the enrolled and not-enrolled examples below distinguishable BY THEIR REQUEST, which is what lets both be tested against a real implementation -- a single account cannot be simultaneously enrolled and not enrolled.

In the seeded demo data acc-0001 is enrolled and acc-0002 is not.

response.name: 404 Not Found - not enrolled

item.name: Ops
item.description: Not a customer purpose. These exist so the harness can prove which blue/green pool served a request, and so the ALB has a health check target.

request.description: ALB target group health check target.
Reports which pool and which build served this request. Without this the harness cannot demonstrate that an atomic listener swap actually moved traffic.
